DUEL SCREEN AIDS (public info only): each stat row shows how many of the rival's REMAINING cards it beats and the run band it would earn against them; spent rival cards grey out; a unit's COACH row is shown on screen as its coach banner; the captain picker shows boosted numbers. DATA: player names are DELIBERATE altered spellings (cartoon lookalikes — licensing rule, not typos). Every number is a real international career line (stats-as-of date on each card); '—' Economy = no wicket-taking bowling in that format (plays as the worst Economy); a low R/A on a bowler is real tail-end batting. RULE DETAIL: Wildcard SWAPS (exchanges, never copies) one stat value between the card you play and another card in your hand for the rest of the over. Review: after a lost ball, cancel it — runs, pot and any wicket undone, both cards stay spent. All out: reaching the unit's wicket limit ends the duel at once as a loss (a rival all out = your win). Aggressive losses are the only way to lose a wicket. SQUAD: fixture hands are the proven default; outside teach units the player may swap 2 cards for cards from their own collection deck.
levels.intent: FINAL: best of three overs — a T20 over, an ODI over and a Test over, each with its own hand; a tied over goes to a Super Over. Fog, Wildcard, Mega Pot, captain and one Review. Aha: you only need two overs — know which format your hand is weakest in and treat that over as the one you can afford to lose.
